n.Navarr: Irra Harah refuses any further aid in Therunin, accusing the Empire of abandoning the weak, young and elderly there. Hayaak's emissary is described as looking like a Navarr or Suaq changeling.
n.The League: A League briar delivers Irra Harah's message, and freelance troublemaker Rafael Barossa d'Apulian is summoned by Janon to fan the flames against Asavea. Kimus sends the herald Fotismos to advise Eilian Sweetwater's Sarvos lighthouse symposium.
n.The Marches: Tharim's knights reached Upwold shortly before the Solstice. Tharim demands a Declaration of Acceptance for Marcher magicians to help his knights hunt Obligatus's killers, and the Civil Service warns this could badly disrupt the Marches.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the framing story follows the Wintermark civil servant Jorgen, and Janon's emissary wears a mix of Winterfolk and Imperial Orc garb.

t.Bay of Catazar: Tharim wishes to discuss the Sunken Rope's attention being drawn to the Bay of Catazar, and offers protection against the Deep and the Dark to any territory whose senator humbles themselves before his Lord-Captain.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is not named on the page, and is at most touched by Tharim's demand to scour the Marches and nearby lands.
t.Sarangrave: Irra Harah names the Sarangrave as the Empire's next test after the Barrens. He will help its orcs and humans run, hide or kill to survive, whoever bears down on them.
t.Sarvos: Kimus has sent her herald Fotismos to the Sarvos lighthouse symposium to advise Eilian Sweetwater. Records recall that the Kindling Cadre aided the former slaves in Sarvos during the Orc Rebellion.
t.Skarsind: Janon's warriors want to discuss the Skarsind College of Pit Fighting with Stonesworn Crix.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Kindling Cadre are recorded as having fought alongside the former slaves in Tassato during the Orc Rebellion.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah calls the Barrens the first test the Empire faced, before the Sarangrave.
t.Therunin: Irra Harah will give no further aid in Therunin, saying the Empire abandoned its weak, young and elderly. He has already helped protect those who remain and said what more is needed.
t.Upwold: Tharim's knights have arrived in Upwold and trouble is brewing. Tharim demands a memorial edifice in the Copse of the Bone Birch where Obligatus was murdered, which might also serve as a fane to him.

r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Imperial armies invading Kroll have encountered the Lake Beast. Generals may beseech Tharim for aid, and he will shield the most deferential general's army from the beast's casualties.

Can't give everything away.d: Ambassador Bedelaar Huisbaas Annike delivered the ultimatum to the Empire and every other nation. Asavea, facing war with the Empire, Sumaah and the Delves, dropped its bounty, so Sarcophan ministry prices should return to normal by the Autumn Equinox. The Delves hoped to keep free trade but accepted the Senate might end it. The wind also set out several openings: Kruidenkenner talks with the Apothecaries Guild, a possible port in Holberg or the draining of the Great Pits of Ennerlund, Hyena investment in the Brass Coast, and market research for Annike. It also covered a strange flower in Hahnmark, a controversial Highborn funerary-goods deal, research into sea eternals, and an offer for black pearls.

n.Highguard: The Council of Benefactors endorsed a deal selling Highborn granite and funerary art to the Sarcophan Collectors, giving every Highborn business and mine 18 extra rings a season until Spring 388YE. The deal also damaged the Cathedral of the Navigators and the Assembly's standing, and two competing mandates were offered to end it.
n.The Brass Coast: After Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo declared the Coast open for business, the Hyena seat showed interest in selling mithril and artisan metals to Freeborn markets. That interest was held back by the threat of the Children of Wrecks, and appraisals, ambassadorial proposals, Autumn magic or private letters were suggested as ways to win investment.
n.The League: Sarcophan interest in a port in Holberg and in draining the Great Pits of Ennerlund remained alive, with Schuyler Koopman staying with the Kleists. If free trade ended, the Delves would focus on the Alivetti estate in Sarvos.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Custodian of the Concordium Dock is listed among the ministries whose Sarcophan prices had risen by a fifth and should now return to normal.
n.Wintermark: A mysterious spiralling flower, draaikolkbloem, began growing among the vlinderbloem cultivated for the Kraft brothers on Hahnmark farms. A Sarcophan vintner offered to brew viezesmaak from any blooms brought to Anvil.

t.Bay of Catazar: Annike dismissed the idea of an eternal physically beneath the Bay but offered to host Imperial historical research into a dangerous Winter eternal tied to the sea. A Sarcophan coven also offered a Mask of the Seven Seas for twelve of the strange black pearls found by captains crossing the Bay.
t.Hahnmark: Farms growing vlinderbloem found a new flower, draaikolkbloem, growing among the crop. Some blamed the Penumbral Veil or the territory's mineral-rich soil, and the Kraft brothers and a Sarcophan vintner were keen to test its worth.
t.Holberg: Koopman remained hopeful of a joint Sarcophan-Imperial port in Holberg, even though the Senate had dropped the appraisal in favour of lighthouses. Hyena families were also interested in helping to drain the Great Pits of Ennerlund if Naomi of Virtue's Rest were asked to appraise it.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan houses were said to be eager to access the Brass Coast's wealth of metals from Kahraman.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Custodian of the Concordium Dock is named among the Sarcophan-supplied ministries hit by the one-fifth price rise, which was expected to ease.
t.Sarvos: The Alivetti estate remained the Delves' foothold in the Empire, and would become their main focus if the Senate abandoned free trade. Freeborn senators had pointedly claimed the Kruidenkenner were not prospering in Sarvos.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Koopman was staying with Bernhard and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund, and the Hyena families were interested in a joint effort to drain the Great Pits of Ennerlund, pending an appraisal.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fisher orcs of Misericorde were said to share Holberg's enthusiasm for a Sarcophan trading port.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Mentioned in passing: the Morass is cited as the kind of marshy terrain where Sarcophan engineers have unmatched experience, which supports the idea of draining the Great Pits.

Construct Ashen Tears Wayhouse.d: Firesong Arachas, the Legion Engineer, announced the construction of a wayhouse named the Ashen Tears in Skogei, Skarsind. The commission called for 16 wains of white granite and 6 thrones (listed among the costs as 16 white granite and 48 crowns), with three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice 387YE, "Grim" Grimmeth Ashen-Tear provided the full 6 thrones and 16 wains of white granite. The wayhouse is now complete, and the title of Keeper of the Ashen Tears becomes available to be appointed by unanimous vote of the senators of Navarr, for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

n.Imperial Orcs: A new wayhouse stands within the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind, announced by the Legion Engineer and funded by Grimmeth Ashen-Tear, though its keeper is chosen by Navarr rather than by the orcs' own senators.
n.Navarr: The Navarr senators gain the right to appoint the Keeper of the Ashen Tears by unanimous vote, first at the Autumn Equinox 387YE, giving Navarr a role at a wayhouse in Skarsind.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind gains the completed Ashen Tears wayhouse, built in Skogei with 16 wains of white granite and 6 thrones.

r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: Skogei Glens is the site of the newly completed Ashen Tears wayhouse, whose keeper will be named by the senators of Navarr.

Construct Barossa University of Dramatur.d: The university would act as a college of magic with the unique power to codify rituals itself or to work with the Doyen of Spires to achieve unprecedented codification. It also creates the League title of Reapers Gift, appointed by auction, responsible for promoting dramaturgy, overseeing the university and facilitating collaboration between Urizen and League magicians. Construction requires 70 white granite, 60 weirwood, 70 mithril and 75 thrones in labour, takes 12 months and carries 12 thrones upkeep. Many citizens donated materials and money between Summer 387YE and Autumn 388YE. The project stemmed from the wind of fortune The play that came to Apulian.

n.The League: The League would gain a new college of magic in Apulian and a new national title, the Reapers Gift, appointed by auction to oversee the university and promote dramaturgy; League citizens supplied much of the material and coin.
n.Urizen: The university is meant to foster collaboration between Urizen and League magicians and may work with the Urizen Doyen of Spires to achieve unprecedented ritual codification.

t.Spiral: Spiral is to host the new Barossa University of Dramaturgical Arts in the city of Apulian, adding a college of magic to the territory.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the motion was announced by the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, who bears the territory's name.

r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus is the site of the planned university in Apulian, with donated weirwood, white granite, mithril and coin flowing in towards its construction.

Construct Carmine Fields Trading Post.d: Proposed by the senator for the Barrens and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion arose from the Little Mercy Wind of Fortune. It cost 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns and took three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Reynard of De Gauvain provided 4 thrones, 2 crowns and 12 wains of weirwood, and Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven gave a crown each. With construction complete, the Envoy to the Karass became available to appoint for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 387YE. The holder is chosen by a Tally of the Votes of Dawnish military unit captains and serves a shortened first term of three seasons.

n.Dawn: Dawn gains a new title, the Envoy to the Karass. It is chosen by the captains of Dawnish military units and was first appointable at the Autumn Equinox 387YE, and a Dawnish noble, Reynard of De Gauvain, supplied most of the funds and all the weirwood.

t.The Barrens: The Barrens' senator proposed the motion, and the new trading post ministry now stands at Carmine Fields in the Barrens, under Dawnish control.

Construct Crystal Fruit Garden.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Mournwold, the motion commissioned a mana sinecure in Serenael costing 12 mithril and 36 crowns, taking three months, and fully self-funded. Grundfos Thorn's Rest supplied the 12 wains of mithril and 4 thrones 4 crowns after the Summer Solstice 387YE. With the work complete, the Keeper of the Crystal Fruit, responsible for coordinating Navarr farmers, was to be appointed annually by unanimous decision of the Navarr senators. The first appointment was set for the Autumn Equinox 387YE, for a reduced term of six months.

n.Navarr: Navarr gained a new title, the Keeper of the Crystal Fruit, to coordinate its farmers, chosen by unanimous agreement of the nation's senators.

t.Miaren: Miaren became home to the Crystal Fruit Garden, a new mana sinecure built in the Navarr-held territory.

r.Miaren/Serenael: The Crystal Fruit Garden was constructed in Serenael and completed after Grundfos Thorn's Rest supplied the mithril and crowns.

Construct Icarion Qanat.d: The motion followed the opportunity described in the Million miles of water wind of fortune. Construction needed 40 wains of weirwood and 144 crowns, a cost raised by Icarion's under-developed state, and took three months. After the Summer Solstice, Irontide Flax gave 30 wains of weirwood and Pathfinder Gaddak gave 2. Karrak, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven each gave a crown, and small donations added 10 rings. After the Autumn Equinox, Irontide Flax gave a further 8 wains of weirwood, Stonesworn Crix gave 17 thrones, 3 crowns and 10 rings, and Karrak another crown. With the qanat complete, Icarion is no longer arid.

n.Grendel: As one of the nations holding Mareave that season, Grendel shares a territory where a new qanat has ended Icarion's arid condition.
n.Imperial Orcs: As one of the nations holding Mareave that season, the Imperial Orcs share a territory where a new qanat has ended Icarion's arid condition.

t.Mareave: Mareave's own senator proposed the qanat, and it now stands in the territory's Icarion region, paid for with weirwood and coin donated by individual citizens.

r.Mareave/Icarion: The qanat was built in Icarion, where its under-developed state raised the cost. Once finished, it removed the region's arid quality.

Construct Jonas' Legacy.d: The tower serves as the residence of the Emerald Arcanist, whose role is to advise the Vallornguard on magical matters and monitor the border with Brocéliande. The holder receives nine mana crystals each season, distilled from a network of mithril bowls built into the tower. The title is Imperial and is elected annually in Autumn by majority vote of the Vallornguard. The motion directed that the Castellan of Spiral Castle pay the costs: 10 mithril and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. Tallis Hart provided 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns after the Summer Solstice. The first Emerald Arcanist could be appointed at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained a new magical tower and Imperial title in its territory of Semmerholm, chosen by the Vallornguard, whose magical advice and watch on the Brocéliande border it strengthens.
n.The League: The motion directed the Castellan of Spiral Castle, in the League's territory of Spiral, to pay the tower's costs.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Emerald Arcanist is charged with monitoring the border with Brocéliande, which the Vallorn held at the time.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm became home to Jonas' Legacy, a tower that produces nine mana crystals each season for the Emerald Arcanist who keeps watch on its border with Brocéliande.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the costs of the tower were to be paid by the Castellan of Spiral Castle.

r.Semmerholm/Elvette: Jonas' Legacy was built in Elvette, with a network of mithril bowls distilling mana for the Emerald Arcanist who lives there.

Construct Prosperous Counting House in H.d: The commission arose from the Forwards and Rewards Wind of Fortune and cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months needed to build. Funding came slowly through donations from many citizens between Summer 387YE and Spring 388YE. Otmar van Holberg, Morgan Townsend von Holberg, Jonah Yakovitch and several others supplied materials, and Sebastian Adolphus von Temeschwar gave 2 thrones 3 crowns. Once complete, the counting house was to provide an additional 15 crowns each season to the Virtue Fund from donations made there, starting at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

n.The League: A League city gained a new civic edifice, largely paid for by League citizens such as the van Holbergs and the Adelaars, which channels donations into the Empire's Virtue Fund.

t.Holberg: The Prosperous Counting House was built in Holberg and, once finished, its donations were to swell the Virtue Fund by 15 crowns a season from Autumn 388YE.

Construct Sermersuaq Spy Network.d: Announced by the Imperial Spymaster under the warning that "the threat of the claw lingers and grows", the commission called for a spy network to be built in Sermersuaq. It cost 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns, with standard costs applying, and was due to take three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice, Aengel Dunn provided 3 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood, and a further 2 crowns came in small donations. Once complete, military units will be able to support the spy network in the territory.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a planned intelligence network in its territory of Sermersuaq, meant to give early warning of the threat the Spymaster called "the claw".

t.Sermersuaq: A spy network was commissioned in Sermersuaq, due to take three months to build, after which military units there will be able to support it.

Construct Silver Fox Mines.d: Alexnadro von Temeschwar, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the opportunity, linked to the Don't blame me Wind of Fortune. The great work was to be named the Silver Fox Mines and sponsored by the Crimson Reapers. It would cost 50 weirwood, 50 white granite and 25 thrones (300 crowns), and take six months to build. Once complete, Temeschwar's mines would yield 36 rings and its businesses two random ingots. The Custodian of the Assayer's Guild would gain two ministry ranks, and taxation from Temeschwar would rise by five thrones a season. Donations came from the Descent Guild of Ore Extraction (12 thrones 4 crowns) and three individuals (one crown each). The commission lapsed before completion.

n.The League: The League was offered a great work in its own territory that would have enriched Temeschwar's mines and businesses and raised its tax yield, but it lapsed with most of its cost still unpaid.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar stood to gain extra rings from its mines, ingots from its businesses and five thrones a season in taxation, but the commission lapsed before it was built.

r.Temeschwar/Locul: Locul was the planned site of the Silver Fox Mines, but the commission lapsed by Summer 388YE without the great work being completed.

Construct Stockland Bounders Hall.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by Miaren, the motion commissioned a Bounders Hall in Stockland at a cost of 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns in labour, taking three months to complete. It arose from the Kith and kin Wind of Fortune. After the Summer Solstice, Henry Birchsmith provided the 12 wains of white granite and Thomas Oak provided 4 thrones and 4 crowns. With the hall complete, the Marcher senators may appoint the Bailiff of the Heath by unanimous decision, first at the Autumn Equinox 387YE for a shortened six-month term. The hall also allows Marcher beaters to send their military units to support the territory.

n.The Marches: The Marcher senators gain a new title, the Bailiff of the Heath, to appoint by unanimous decision, and Marcher beaters may now send their military units to support Upwold. The hall was funded by prosperous Marcher citizens, among them Henry Birchsmith and Thomas Oak.

t.Upwold: A Bounders Hall now stands in Stockland, providing a base from which Marcher beaters can send their military units to support the territory.

Construct the Dreaming Spire.d: Announced by Lucrezia Corvinascura, Chair of the Wolf, the commission celebrated two years of friendship and the completion of the League's reckoning with Urizen. It offered a home for the Omphalos, the Library of Solen's Doubt and all Urizen Spiralites. The work needed 26 wains of white granite and labour costs. Several citizens contributed money between Summer and Autumn 387YE, and Raine Tealeaf supplied 25 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice, which completed the spire. On completion, any Urizen could take a new personal resource in Spiral for free until the close of downtime after the Spring Equinox 388YE. The Urizen Assembly would appoint the new Custodian of the Omphalos for the first time at that Equinox.

n.The League: The League's premier building society, Red Raven Holdings, commissioned the spire as a gift to its Urizen neighbours in League-held Spiral, and the League's Chair of the Wolf announced it.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained a home in Spiral for the Omphalos and the Library of Solen's Doubt. Any Urizen could take a free personal resource in Spiral after completion, and the Urizen Assembly would appoint the new Custodian of the Omphalos to uphold Urizen culture there.

t.Spiral: Spiral, held by the League, received a new edifice that serves as a cultural heart for its Urizen inhabitants, and it opened to new Urizen personal resources for a limited time.

r.Spiral/Ankra: The Dreaming Spire was raised on Mount Cinnius in Ankra and now houses the Omphalos of Urizen and the Library of Solen's Doubt.

Daybreak in Spiral.d: After Ylenwe was granted Amity, the Dawn Chorus arrived and settled at Solen's Doubt. Its song silences the Black Plateau's whispers but can confuse attackers. Ylenwe's heralds offered captains supporting the dam-building army a feather that works like a Circlet of Falling Snow. Carving the Imperial Orcs' fallen into the dam would add five thrones, and relocating Solen's Doubt's library to a new Dreaming Spire another five; both must be settled in the dam's commission. The omphalos lies on Mount Lutum in Iteri or Mount Cinnius in Ankra, depending on whether Spiral is counted. The heralds visited the Block, held by the Silver Flame rebels. Their leader Caela asked the Conclave for a Declaration of Concord granting them Imperial Lore.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the rebels are said to be no more Urizeni than the so-called Earl of the Groves is Dawnish.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Urizeni are once again fighting to keep the Druj from their homes in north-east Zenith.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Solen's Doubt was the site of a decisive battle against the Grendel, and the opening story features a Lost orc once of that nation.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly's demand to carve the names of the fallen into the dam can be met for an extra five thrones. Whoever commissions the dam must state whether this will be done, and the orcs are likely to object if it is not.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls the bitter days when the League took Spiral and nation seemed set to war against nation.
n.Urizen: Halkyon's statement inspired a call to found a Dreaming Spire at the nation's omphalos, which would preserve Solen's Doubt's library and let Urizeni take new resources there. Meanwhile the Silver Flame rebels, no longer bound by the egregore, seek Imperial Lore their people helped to build.

t.Mareave: The planned dam on the Doubt is part of the effort to relieve the aridity of Mareave's Icarion region.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is one of the territories counted when scholars calculate the geographic centre of Urizen.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt counts in the omphalos calculation, and its spires trade and cooperate with the Silver Flame rebels.
t.Spiral: The Dawn Chorus and Ylenwe's heralds now soothe parts of the cursed land, a Dreaming Spire may be founded in Ankra, and the rebels holding the Block in Cinion are seeking Imperial Lore.
t.Zenith: Mount Lutum in Iteri is one candidate site for the Dreaming Spire. Halkyon's words resonate strongly in north-east Zenith, where the Urizeni are fighting the Druj.

r.Mareave/Icarion: Damming the River Doubt is intended to relieve Icarion's aridity.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Mount Cinnius in Ankra, on the border with Cinion, is the omphalos if Spiral is counted part of Urizen, and the Silver Flame would support a spire built there.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The Dawn Chorus settled at the ruined spire of Solen's Doubt, which would sit at the centre of the planned reservoir, and Ylenwe's heralds descended from a spring above Apstrus.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Ylenwe's heralds traced the Block to Cinion and, after tense talks brokered by a herald of That Which Lives In Its Name, were allowed to visit it under the Silver Flame rebels' watch.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Mount Lutum in Iteri, where Spire Calator once stood, is the omphalos if Urizen is counted as Zenith, Redoubt and Morrow, making it a possible site for the Dreaming Spire.

Eight for a wish.d: A magnitude 20 Autumn projection was offered to help many citizens join the sodality, followed by the election of a Speaker. The Constitutional Court found the Advisor on the Vallorn unconstitutional as it stood, and the title was redefined to be appointed by the Vallornguard. It later gained the power to address the Military Council. The sodality was not granted appraisal, the appointment of generals, or fortification powers. The League's mandate created a 10-throne bequest. The Burgher of Ketsov became Vallornguard-appointed. Highguard's mandate raised white granite donations to twelve wains. The third Navarr army and the Boyar of the Iron Roads were left unchanged. Conjunctions targeted a Druj vallorn cult in Brocéliande and the lost Vate's Shelter in Bendol.

n.Dawn: The Knight of the Greenwood, Percival Summerstrong, was made responsible for reclaiming Vate's Shelter in Bendol, and several Dawnish nobles and knights supported the Defence of the Broch.
n.Druj: At least three hundred orcs have embraced life within the vallorn in Dark Ranging and are attacking the Broch's wayhouses. Another Druj party is hunting the lost Vate's Shelter among vallornspawn husks in Bendol.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr guide cynically lists beating the Grendel among the fronts the Empire must stabilise before it fights the vallorn.
n.Highguard: The Highborn National Assembly enacted a mandate backing a Vigilant approach, raising white granite donations to the Benefactors' Council from ten to twelve wains. The Stone Aerie's fortification plan was not adopted, as the sodality was not given the power to commission fortifications. The Greenwatcher might yet seek Lord Rain's patronage for the sodality.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are named among the enemies the Empire would need to deal with before turning on the vallorn.
n.Navarr: The Advisor on the Vallorn, a Navarr-appointed title, was redefined to be appointed by the Vallornguard. The proposal to hand the new third Navarr army, and with it the Thornbound Steading's support, to the sodality was not taken up. Some Navarr saw the sodality as an insult, while others saw it as their best hope.
n.The League: The League Assembly enacted the mandate repurposing Lorenzo La Volpe's gallery, museum and theatre to fund the Vallornguard. They no longer supply liao to priests, and instead provide a bequest of 10 thrones each season.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the fronts the Empire might need to beat if no deal can be struck with them.
n.Varushka: The Burgher of Ketsov became a Varushkan title appointed by the Vallornguard, which kept the Ketsov ministry working. The proposed expansion of the Boyar of the Iron Roads' powers was not made.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the inspiration of the Sentinel was once used to help defend the Empire against barbarians along the Bay of Catazar.
t.Brocéliande: Over a thousand knights and thorns entered the forests hunting Druj who had embraced the vallorn. The Speaker of the Vallornguard was made responsible for killing the cult's leaders to save the Broch spy network.
t.Casinea: The Stone Aerie chapter founded at the Silent Sentinel proposed helping the Vallornguard build fortifications against the vallorn, and the Greenwatch's link to Lord Rain was raised as a possible source of support.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr guide fears Hercynia could be abandoned to the vallorn within ten or twenty years.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr guide counts Liathaven among the places already lost.
t.Ossium: The Ketsov of Ossium withdrew support from the Burgher of Ketsov in protest, and the Senate made the title appointed by the Vallornguard so its ministry could continue.
t.Sarangrave: While Imperial armies clashed with the Druj here, sodality scouts tracked a Druj party into Bendol searching for the lost Vate's Shelter.
t.Sarvos: Congregations here lose the extra liao from Lorenzo's cultural institutions, whose patronage was redirected to fund the Vallornguard.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Civil Service's arcane projection for joining the sodality was presented to Semmerholm's senator, Amicia of the Semmerlak.
t.Tassato: Congregations here lose the extra liao from Lorenzo's cultural institutions, whose patronage was redirected to fund the Vallornguard.
t.Temeschwar: Home of Lorenzo La Volpe's Bloody Butchers Guild. Its congregations lose the extra liao from his institutions, now turned to fundraising for the Vallornguard.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: its abandonment to the vallorn is lamented, and the situation there leaves Lord Rain's relationship with the Empire in the balance.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: The Druj and the herald of Yaw'nagrah who fled here in 385YE have grown into a vallorn-embracing cult of at least three hundred orcs, now targeted by the Lose the Sun conjunction.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The Abraxus Stone Vate's Shelter was lost in the miasma here. The Portion of Wisdom conjunction tasked the Knight of the Greenwood with claiming it before the Druj could recover it.

For those in peril on the sea.d: Cyrus, senator for Reikos, seconded by Pathfinder Gaddak of Mareave, asked for the appraisal to guard against new eternal threats and restore national Pride. Experts from the Brass Coast, League, Highguard, Urizen and the Unshackled met in Sarvos, joined by Fotismos, herald of Kimus. Plans for lighthouse edifices and fleet-boosting great lighthouses were made available. The Shining Pillar cannot be rebuilt because a maelstrom has devoured its island. The Celesti Lighthouse could instead be restored, or rebuilt as a fortified great lighthouse that lifts Oranseri's abandoned quality, and Kimus offers an infused light enabling a Bay patrol voyage and the Broken Shore Bounty. Eilian asks the Senate to approve a year-long sabbatical to study further sites.

n.Grendel: Sannite delegates said the Grendel prize lighthouses, with Salt Lords paying their keepers, and that Rahab's endorsement of the looting of the Celesti Lighthouse troubled traditional Grendel lords. An infused Celesti light would remind Grendel navies of Freeborn defiance.
n.Highguard: Highborn architects joined the symposium, recalling the lost Pharos of Necropolis as a symbol of Vigilance. Their tower-building skill and Highguard warning bells feature in the fortified Celesti proposal.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Unshackled of Mareave attended, newly appreciative of lighthouses now that they hold a coastline. They pointed to the ruined lighthouse at Icarion and a smaller one above the docks at Beoraidh.
n.The Brass Coast: Lighthouses carry near-spiritual meaning for the Freeborn, and the loss of the Shining Pillar and the Celesti Lighthouse hurt corsair families deeply. The proposals would restore the Celesti Lighthouse, its Keeper title and possibly the Broken Shore Bounty.
n.The League: League delegates valued lighthouses as practical symbols of Prosperity and their mirror-masters claim unrivalled skill. The unbuilt Caricomare lighthouse of Sarvos is one of the six sites proposed for further study.
n.Urizen: An Urizen speaker championed lighthouses as symbols of illumination and sanctuary, and Urizen lightstone craft is essential to great beacons. The lost Lighthouse of Nikephoros and the lighthouses of Naris are both candidates for Eilian's further study.

t.Bay of Catazar: The appraisal surveyed the Bay's lost great lighthouses amid fears that an unknown eternal threat lurks in its depths. A Kimus-infused Celesti light would create a Patrol the Bay of Catazar voyage that also reports unusual events at sea.
t.Feroz: The Celesti Lighthouse at Oran could be restored, or rebuilt as a fortified great lighthouse that boosts Feroz-based fleets and lets fleets guard its coastal waters. An infused version would strengthen divinations against shrouds over the territory.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Celesti monastery near the Gilded Peak holds the archived plans for the lighthouse's golden lamp.
t.Madruga: The famed Shining Pillar cannot be restored, because its island is held by the Children of Wrecks and has been swallowed by a perpetual maelstrom.
t.Mareave: The ruined Light of Virtue at Icarion is one of the six sites proposed for further study, and a smaller lighthouse still stands at Beoraidh. Pathfinder Gaddak of Mareave seconded the original request.
t.Necropolis: The territory was once called Pharos after its great lighthouse, burned in the civil war and never rebuilt. That site is a candidate for future study, and Reumah's Rest inspired the fortified Celesti design.
t.Redoubt: The destroyed Lighthouse of Nikephoros, said to stand on a Winter regio, and the lighthouses of Naris near the restored port of Elos are both proposed for further study.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Cyrus, senator for Reikos, proposed the appraisal.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos hosted the week-long lighthouse symposium, and its never-built Caricomare lighthouse, meant partly to protect the city from storms, is a candidate for further study.
t.Spiral: The pre-Imperial Lighthouse of Apulian, the Eye of Kimus, destroyed by Hadrian of Apulian, is one of the six sites proposed for further study.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: the Children of Wrecks' continued control of the Cazar Straits is why Eilian proposes a fortified lighthouse, and the old Celesti beacon once guided ships through Cazar's isles and sandbanks.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Both Celesti Lighthouse commissions would be built here. The fortified version would defend the region, let fleets guard it from the sea and remove its abandoned quality, encouraging Freeborn to resettle Oran.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Shining Pillar once stood here but is now destroyed. Its island has been devoured by a maelstrom said to open into Siakha's realm, so it cannot be rebuilt.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: a smaller lighthouse stands above the docks, and Beoraidh's bazaars gossip about Rahab's looting of the Celesti Lighthouse.
r.Mareave/Icarion: The ruined Light of Virtue, built in an old Urizen style on the clifftops, is a site Eilian is keen to revisit and a candidate for further study.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: The great Pharos stood on these cliffs until it was burned in the civil war. Eilian believes a rebuilt lighthouse here could draw strength from its link to Atuman.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Naris holds the destroyed Lighthouse of Nikephoros and the lighthouses linked to the port of Elos, both proposed for study, with the herald Fotismos especially interested.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: The Caricomare lighthouse planned here was never built because of economic realities, and it is a candidate for Eilian's further study.

Fortify Ruicraic's Redoubt.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by the senator for Mareave, the motion was to be fully funded by the Imperial Orc nation with help from Reumah's Redoubt. It cost 50 white granite, 30 weirwood and 36 thrones, the price raised by the under-developed nature of Icarion, with 8 thrones upkeep and six months to build. Ehud and Karrak supplied most of the materials and money after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox, with crowns from Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven. Ruicraic's Redoubt now stands in Eoradal and could also serve as an embassy to Skoura if that foreign nation agrees.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named in the motion, which concerns Mareave, a territory Grendel shared control of that season.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc nation pledged to fund the fortification in full, and orc contributors such as Ehud and Karrak supplied the granite, weirwood and thrones that saw Ruicraic's Redoubt completed.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the motion names Reumah's Redoubt as helping the Imperial Orcs fund the work, and Urizen is otherwise not mentioned.

t.Mareave: Mareave gained a new rank one fortification, Ruicraic's Redoubt in Eoradal, which could also serve as an embassy to Skoura if that nation agrees.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the only link is the name Reumah's Redoubt, cited as helping to fund the work, and nothing is built or decided in the Redoubt.

r.Mareave/Eoradal: Ruicraic's Redoubt was raised in Eoradal and now stands there as a rank one fortification.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Mentioned in passing: the under-developed nature of Icarion is cited as raising the cost of the project to 36 thrones.

Here comes the night.d: The army was raised by a Winter Solstice 386YE motion proposed for Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad and seconded by Myshki Marishka Letuchaya. Cabal Lyktan's Hammers of Fury enchantments sped its mustering. Most Varushkans did not want the lost Iron Helms recreated. The options were the conquering quality inspired by Ratibor of Temeschwar, the foraging quality of the wagon raiders, and the sell sword quality, which required a Hound's Hall. Sovereign offers included the Dubik (bloodthirsty, needing a shrine in Suvretz), the Charnel Lord (Branoc born), the Howling Queen (accursed), and a rumoured bargain with the Night Below. Aleksandr chose the name Boyar's Hasta and backed the wagon raiders and sell swords. The Hound's Hall was built and the Sell Sword quality took effect.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Morrigan Mortere of Dawn was asked to host, at the Mortere camp, a meeting between Varushkans and a servant of the Charnel Lord.
n.Druj: The new Varushkan army was raised to take the fight to the Druj, and those inspired by Ratibor hoped it would end their threat for good by claiming their lands.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a young Varushkan recruit hoped that Reinos, then held by the Jotun, would be assigned to Varushka once claimed.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the schlacta recalled Varushka's oath to stand with the Navarr against the vallorn, and the Iron Helms' final orders spoke of finishing the work in Therunin.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League was cited as the only nation with a stronger mercenary tradition than Varushka.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained its third army, Boyar's Hasta, which drew on the nation's wagon raiders and sell swords through a newly built Hound's Hall. The bargains offered by the Dubik, the Charnel Lord, the Howling Queen and the Night Below were all passed over.

t.Karov: The new army was raised in Karov, where Cabal Lyktan's Hammers of Fury hastened its mustering. Delev was one of the proposed sites for the Hound's Hall.
t.Karsk: The army's raising senator, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, was the former Senator for Karsk and chose its name and quality. Ivarsgard was one of the proposed sites for the Hound's Hall.
t.Ossium: The success of Ossium's Stinking Market was cited as evidence of Varushkan appetite for raiding, and Karantzy was one of the proposed sites for the Hound's Hall.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: a recruit hoped Reinos would be assigned to Varushka when it was claimed.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Ratibor, boyar of Temeschwar, inspired the proposed conquering quality, which was not chosen.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' final orders spoke of finishing the work in Therunin by eradicating the Druj there.
t.Volodmartz: The Dubik was said to slumber beneath Volodmartz's soil, and its offer of patronage would have required a shrine there. The offer lapsed when the army took a different quality.

r.Karsk/Branoc: Mentioned in passing: the Charnel Lord's patronage would have made the army Branoc born, but this was not chosen.
r.Volodmartz/Suvretz: A Shrine of the Dubik was proposed at an abandoned outpost in eastern Suvretz, all that remained of the old vale of Krastavya. The opportunity was lost when the army took the Sell Sword quality.

Hope and fear.d: With no prognosticator assigned, Gerard La Salle coaxed Mladen Escovitch out of retirement for one last job. Mladen found that each Druj army is supplied by its sept's lands, so completely conquering every region of a territory puts its armies out of supply, though emergency resupply with weirwood or mithril and sept relocation remain possible. He rejected costly alternatives and noted that slaughtering Druj subjects would work but was politically unpalatable. He offered to appraise such cruel strategies if the Senate asks explicitly. He would return to full service, at ten thrones a season, only if the Assembly of Nine passed a judgement with a greater majority and the Senate requested an appraisal that same season.

n.Druj: The appraisal maps which sept supplies each of thirteen Druj armies. It identifies the Salt Flats of Sanath as their political heartland, whose fall alongside one other territory would end the rule of the Buruk Tepel.
n.Grendel: Mladen suggests the Grendel might raid and loot collapsing Druj holdings in Sanath, possibly eyeing eastern islands for weirwood, though he has little experience of them and notes they do not supply armies the Druj way.
n.Highguard: Mladen cites the Stone Toad sept, whose army went out of supply after the Empire reclaimed Reikos and was converted into a garrison in High Chalcis, as evidence for his supply analysis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are said to support more armies than any nation outside the Imperial Orcs might normally manage.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Mladen has little experience fighting the Jotun and is certain they do not supply their armies as the Druj do.
n.Thule: Mladen speculates the Thule might try to extend their dominion into the Forest of Ulnak if the Druj collapsed, though he cautions they do not supply their armies as the Druj do.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen armies are cited as a recent example of an entire nation's armies going out of supply.
n.Varushka: The appraisal was written by Mladen Escovitch, a Varushkan schlacta and former general of the Golden Axe who spent years fighting the Druj. He hopes to retire to his family in Miekarova.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Five Druj armies, from the Iron Asp, Sawscaled Viper and relocated Amber Scorpion septs, draw supply here, and completely conquering every region would leave them in insufficient supply.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Mladen Escovitch intends to return to his family in Miekarova once his work is done.
t.Ossium: The surviving Amber Scorpion sept fled Ossium to the Forest of Ulnak, while the Bone Serpent were wiped out by other Druj when they tried to flee, and the septs of Ossium helped Mladen identify Druj armies.
t.Reikos: After the Empire reclaimed Reikos, the Stone Toad army lost its supplying fiefs there and was converted into a garrison in High Chalcis rather than collapse.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Five armies are supplied from the Salt Flats, and complete conquest would also sever the link between the Sarangrave and the Forest of Ulnak, with the loss of this heartland plus one other territory bringing down the Druj.
t.Sarangrave: Three Druj armies from the Banded Snake, Marshlizard and Thornwasp septs are supplied here, and the Axou would likely leap at the chance to overrun the territory if the Druj collapsed.

I wish you would.d: The Senate passed the Thule treaty, but the General Assembly faced a judgement of veto; if the treaty failed, war with Otkodov would resume after the Summer Solstice. The Thule enchanted and strengthened their fortifications in the Silver Peaks, Crow's Ridge, Miechernya, Krevsaty and the Bonewood, and warded the Webwood. A Thule consortium's cattle were stranded at Crow's Ridge. The Suranni reported a Dumon curse on Arbonne (Kalino) and warned of black pearls in the Bay. Morajasse's Grendel demanded recognition as foreigners. Beoraidh offered land for a temple or basilica and sought investment in a new arena. Skoura raised no objection to weirwood trade with Tsark and sent traders to Anvil.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to the Grendel, Finna of Dawn, handles Grendel negotiations and is invited to meet Wind Lord Morath at the Black Sand Tower.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Sage of Tsark travelling to Anvil was forced to retreat after running afoul of the Druj in Zenith, and the Webwood is described as largely untouched since Druj rule.
n.Grendel: The Grendel stayed at war but quiet, claimed to have dealt with the Children of Wrecks at the Tempest Jade Temple, and offered a meeting with Wind Lord Morath. Commander Gallum's soldiers at Mora's Rock demanded recognition of Morajasse as a foreign protectorate.
n.Imperial Orcs: A Skouran delegation from the Geltcourse Trade Security Council planned to visit the Imperial Orc camp to buy forest resources and discuss long-term trade with the Senator for Mareave.
n.The Brass Coast: The Grendel of Mora's Rock demanded that Bakar and the Seaglass Beacon cease cursing Morajasse, offering protection of the Feroz coast against the Children of Wrecks in return. The Suranni also urged checks that a Dumon-style curse does not strike Segura or Feroz.
n.The Marches: Thule cattle wranglers collected cows bought at Upwold markets, and Suranni historians were so impressed by the Marchers that Baroness Katerine proposed a visit to observe their harvest festival, perhaps as guests of the Garamond household.
n.Thule: The Thule considered their treaty settled but threatened renewed war if it was vetoed. They enchanted and expanded their five fortifications inside the Empire, and their Company of the Icebound Wind was left with cattle exposed at Crow's Ridge.
n.Urizen: Vossk of Zenith Ascendent was specifically invited to meet Wind Lord Morath, while a Tsark sage was driven back by the Druj in Zenith. The Grendel are noted as having been rebuffed from Redoubt.
n.Varushka: Thule fortifications in Miechernya, Krevsaty and the Bonewood were enchanted and strengthened, and the Webwood was warded. Rak invited Senator Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh to write again so Thule and Varushkans might pool knowledge of a threat in the Webwood.
n.Wintermark: The Citadel of Bone and Silver in the Silver Peaks was enchanted and reinforced, and Rak commended Isolde Tempest Shield over the madness in the north-west. Marko Siwarsbairn was a guest of Baroness Katerine, researching Suranni military history until at least Autumn.

t.Bay of Catazar: Strange bells were heard across much of the Bay, and the Suranni warned that black pearls pulled from its waters were blasphemous tools of Dumon. Beoraidh feared attacks by the Children of Wrecks.
t.Feroz: The Grendel of Mora's Rock offered to protect the Feroz coast from the Children of Wrecks if Morajasse was recognised as theirs and the curses stopped, and threatened rituals of their own in Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the hilly terrain of Hahnmark slowed the Thule cattle drive north.
t.Kalino: Known to the Suranni as the Duchy of Arbonne, it was struck by a curse blamed on the Hand of Dumon: weeds, orchard blight, vermin, and sickness that left bark-like scabs.
t.Karsk: The Thule fortification of Krevsatyzmei, watching over Oloy, was enchanted; massive pale wolves were reported watching the southern border.
t.Mareave: Beoraidh fortified itself and offered land for a temple or basilica of the Way. Skouran traders crossed the territory, once their land of Mahal, seeking to meet its Senator.
t.Miekarova: Eldfell, securing Ustyma's Gate, was enchanted with ice and unseasonable snow and reinforced by bear-like servants likely of Cathan Canae.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Skoura raised no objection to Imperial weirwood trade with Tsark but warned that Tsark's motives are philosophical rather than economic; a Tsark sage hoped to attend the Autumn Equinox.
t.Ossium: The Thule reinforced Fljajokep and the Silent Pines in the Bonewood and laid a probable night ward in the Webwood, where a malign threat may be investigated jointly with Varushka.
t.Otkodov: The Thule homeland awaited the treaty's fate. Rak planned to retire if it passed, and the Empire's maps of Otkodov remained poor, with even Verthandi's nearly six years out of date.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel have been notably quiet since being rebuffed from Redoubt.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Baroness Katerine suggested the Empire investigate to ensure a curse like Arbonne's does not happen in Segura.
t.Sermersuaq: The Citadel of Bone and Silver was enchanted and its Stonefield Ice Caves defences improved, and a large Thule force passed through to collect cattle from the Marches.
t.Shavronne: Mentioned in passing: a citizen's past life vision of being a cousin to the Duke of Shavronne prompted Baroness Katerine to advise keeping the matter quiet.
t.Skarsind: Crow's Keep was expanded to a rank two fortification and enchanted, and the Thule cattle herd camped at Crow's Ridge could be seized back if war broke out.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Thule bought their cattle from the markets of Upwold.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat in Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: it is the only Otkodov territory the Empire has mapped, and that map is almost six years old.
t.Zenith: A Sage of Tsark bound for Anvil was forced to retreat from the Druj in Zenith, hoping to come in Autumn if the Druj threat was not imminent.

r.Feroz/Morajasse: Commander Gallum Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse asked the Senate to recognise Morajasse as a protectorate under their command, with its people declared foreigners, and to end Bakar's curses there.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Mentioned in passing: before the Spring Equinox, Gallum's troops fought the Children of Wrecks in Oranseri.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Krevsatyzmei was enchanted; pale wolves larger than oxen were said to stalk the wooded hills watching the southern border.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Lord Ehsan spent mithril strengthening the city's walls and harbour and offered quayside land for a temple or basilica of the Way, while the Diamant Drakes sought Imperial bonds to rebuild the colosseum.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Attempts to establish farms in barren Sinfoyard were going badly, and a proposed shrine in Beoraidh would also preach to its orcs.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Eldfell was iced over and garrisoned with bear-like figures, and Rak warned the Dragons might act themselves if the Falconer's madness kept troubling Miechernya.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Fljajokep was seriously reinforced and bound with glowing brass sigils, with bronze four-armed creatures supplementing the garrison and extra defences at the Silent Pines grove.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Reports told of magic seething in the forest's depths, spawning shadowy shapes, probably a Thule night ward. Rak offered to pass Varushkan concerns about a malign threat there to his warlocks.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Citadel of Bone and Silver was improved and enchanted with glowing runes and drake-like guardians, and the region was among those troubled by the Falconer's madness.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Keep was expanded and enchanted, and the Company of the Icebound Wind's cattle were camped here, open to seizure by a victorious Imperial general if war came.
r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: Mentioned in passing: the expanded Crow's Keep is visible from parts of the Skogei Glens.

Know your enemy.d: The mandate passed by over a thousand votes but without a greater majority, so it was ineffective in Urizen, Varushka and Wintermark, where heresy is now more likely to take deep root. Three Peace-hallowed relics remain with Synod figures, and Cardinal of Wisdom Silas of the Cenotaph has not stepped down. Doubts about this threaten the credibility of the Assembly of Nine and of the other assemblies. The Silent Bell now answers to the Vigilance Assembly and could investigate one false virtue each season. The options are spying on Faraden for Vengeance, Axos for Peace, the Iron Confederacy for Freedom, Urizeni sword scholars for Hatred or the Druj for Fear. Every option carries serious risk of capture. Wintermark's own mandate has left it outside other assemblies' influence unless they reach a greater majority.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named; its only link is the Barrens, where the Freedom Heresy rebels once tried to found a nation of the free.
n.Druj: The Silent Bell could be sent into the Mallum to learn how the Druj create and understand Fear, but most of the spies would certainly be caught and brutally executed.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; it holds Feroz, where the Suranni were once invited to reclaim escaped slaves.
n.Highguard: Historically, many Highborn embraced Purity (Hatred) and some refused to give it up. Constant vigilance is still needed against it in Highguard, with notable failures reaching the top of Highborn society, and Caleb of the Cenotaph's commissioned research on Hatred is available across the Empire.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are named as the foe that the people of Whittle used Hatred to fight, and as the object of a hypothetical Marcher priest's hatred.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: it notes that even the Navarr members of the Silent Bell would struggle to infiltrate the hidden Montanian survivors.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are cited as a place where Hatred has history, from Whittle's reliance on it to old household grudges that the Marcher Assembly denounces.
n.Urizen: Because of its scepticism towards the Synod, the mandate had no effect in Urizen, and heresy there is now more likely to put down deep roots. Severus of the Blinding Sun is already preaching Hatred across its citadels, and the Silent Bell could be sent to spy on such sword scholars in the mountains at grave personal risk.
n.Varushka: The mandate had no effect in Varushka, leaving its people more open to false virtues and heresy that would be hard to uproot. The page also recalls that Varushkans destroyed the Montanian sept.
n.Wintermark: After the Wintermark Assembly urged its people to heed only the stormcrows, Wintermark ignores other assemblies' mandates unless they reach a greater majority. It is therefore more vulnerable to false virtues unless the Wintermark Assembly enacts its own mandate, with its own liao, urging people to bring malign auras to the stormcrows.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is recalled as the place where the Empire invited the Suranni to reclaim escaped slaves inspired by a Freedom-embracing leader.
t.Kalino: The escaped slaves who followed a leader devoted to Freedom are believed to be held, most likely in Kalino, after being dragged back there in chains. The Silent Bell could seek them out, though captured spies would be executed and relations with the Iron Confederacy reversed.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow appears only in the opening story, where Lucia is said to be good enough to cross swords with its best scholars.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold is recalled through the people of Whittle, who relied on Hatred to fight the Jotun and are now gone after failed reintegration.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens are recalled as where the Freedom Heresy rebels settled and where their descendants, the Montanians, later lived until their destruction.

Long grass and stormclouds.d: Children of Wrecks pirates increasingly preyed on Bay of Catazar shipping, while Freeborn corsairs, stretched by missionary runs to Asavea, struggled to protect it. Grendel privateer attacks declined and Grendel armies were largely unseen. In Feroz the Grendel garrison at Mora's Rock held its borders amid rumours of diplomacy. Wintermark's Fist of the Mountains and the Freeborn Burning Falcon reclaimed the eerily silent Quiet Grasses, making Madruga Imperial again for the Senate to assign. The Gathered Storm, traitor corsairs under Isidore i Boyaga and Ioan Bloodstride's false Navarr attacked Trivento but were repelled by the Great Chain and Our Lady of Pride before abruptly withdrawing south.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the School of Imperial Strategy warns that the Children of Wrecks, if unchecked, could rival the Druj for the damage they inflict on the Empire.
n.Grendel: Their privateers attacked Imperial ships less often, their armies stayed silent after clearing the Imperial inroad into Ayereed, and their Feroz garrison held Morajasse. Meanwhile Grendel companies backed Asavean scouts in Necropolis, funded the Courath of Icarion and guarded a cache for the Brine Turtles in Mareave.
n.Highguard: Necropolis faced Grendel-escorted Asavean scouts probing its defences while the Shamal lay anchored offshore, and the General of the Citadel Guard was charged with defeating the Courath of Icarion in Mareave.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skywise Gralka is named as one of those whose statements of principle drew researchers to Mareave, where Grendel agents were active.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the traitor Ioan Bloodstride is described as a refugee from a lost striding in Liathaven, now held by the Jotun.
n.Navarr: A false-steading called Liath's Blade, half Navarr traitors and half Imperial dregs posing as Navarr, attacked Trivento's defenders from behind under Ioan Bloodstride before being forced back.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs were stretched protecting the Bay, the Burning Falcon helped reclaim the Quiet Grasses, and Madruga was expected, though not guaranteed, to be reassigned to the Brass Coast. Traitor corsairs under Isidore i Boyaga joined the raid on Trivento.
n.The League: League defenders, backed by the Great Chain and Our Lady of Pride, repelled the Children of Wrecks at Trivento, though the town suffered burned ships and looted businesses and strategists warned a full assault might succeed.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains, with Janon's subdued mystics and Winter-raised dead of Tassato, helped reclaim the Quiet Grasses, where soldiers whispered that the undead were growing more aware and menacing.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel removed the minor Imperial inroad into Ayereed and then went silent.
t.Bay of Catazar: Children of Wrecks attacks on shipping rose steadily while Grendel privateer raids declined, leaving overstretched Freeborn corsairs in a tense balance with the pirates.
t.Feroz: Wind Lord Saoirse and Commander Fiersach kept their forces at Mora's Rock without clashing with the Freeborn, amid rumours of correspondence with Imperial citizens.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Ioan Bloodstride, leader of the false Navarr who attacked Trivento, came from a lost striding in Liathaven.
t.Madruga: With the Quiet Grasses retaken, Madruga became an Imperial territory again despite the magical marsh and the Children of Wrecks' hold on the island, and the Senate was to decide its assignment.
t.Mareave: Two conjunctions arose here: the Courath of Icarion meeting Grendel paymasters while wielding Stormcaller, and a Grendel company guarding a resource cache intended for the Brine Turtles.
t.Necropolis: The Shamal stayed anchored off the coast, and Grendel escorting servants of the Red God scouted for weaknesses, a threat the Champion of Pride was charged to counter.
t.Sarvos: Trivento withstood a huge raid by the Children of Wrecks and their traitor allies, suffering damage but preventing a loss of the territory's taxation.
t.Segura: The Grendel garrison did not raid Segura, and Freeborn warbands found an old road that, with some work, could serve as a caravan pass from the Quiet Grasses into Segura.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's undead were raised from the dead of Tassato, and the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy there studied the Trivento battle.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: named as a Children of Wrecks holding that nothing appeared to threaten when their fleet broke off.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Grendel still controlled Morajasse, with Imperial and Grendel forces watching its borders but no fighting.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: named as a Children of Wrecks holding that nothing appeared to threaten when their fleet broke off.
r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: The restored, Winter-touched grassland of towering, resilient grass and strange silence was reclaimed for the Empire by the Fist of the Mountains and the Burning Falcon, and an old road was found for caravans.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: its drinking houses are cited as places buzzing with speculation about the Children of Wrecks.
r.Mareave/Icarion: The Courath of Icarion, bearing the Grendel-supplied artefact Stormcaller, threatened to become an entrenched rebel presence unless defeated by the General of the Citadel Guard.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Longbeach would come under Grendel threat if the Asavean scouts escorted by Grendel reported back successfully to the Salt Lords.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: The Children of Wrecks assaulted Trivento's harbour and gates, but mithril chains, watchtowers and the garrison drove them off, leaving burned ships and raided businesses.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Mentioned in passing: its coast was among those fortified with watchtowers as part of the Great Chain defences.

Nightfall in Apulian.d: Five dramaturgical personae (all but the Mountebank) now appeared openly in Apulian. Its streets shifted unpredictably, favouring pleasure and subterfuge, though the Black Plateau seemed unaffected. Proposals for an Academy or University of Dramaturgy had popular support. Teodore duSesna of the DuSesna Guild accused Rafael Barossa, Genoveva Barossa, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato and Sofonisba Amilcara of complicity in a pact with Sung through the Chamber of Euphony. Few believed him, but Synod scrutiny was suggested. Victo von Temeschwar revealed a single Grendel ring across the Bay of Catazar. The Senate could guarantee destruction of the Spiral jewel, or the Military Council could gamble on luring or deterring Grendel attacks.

n.Grendel: The Salt Council's bribery-and-blackmail espionage ring was exposed, and its Spiral jewel could be destroyed or used to feed them false intelligence. This could lure their armies into attacking Spiral or scare them away for two seasons.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Barachel of Adina's Charge was recalled as having uncovered Grendel spies in Necropolis, and the Senate's refusal to restore Berechiah's Basilica in Bastion was noted.
n.The League: League citizens of Apulian could draw on the manifest personae and gain strength in Night magic, while prominent League figures of the Camorra Barossa were publicly accused over Sung's fane.
n.Urizen: Urizeni magicians, backed by an Urizen Assembly statement, were eager to study Apulian's dramaturgical confluence, and Urizen characters from Spiral could share in the city's magical effects.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: a proper restoration of Berechiah's Basilica there, with a Clavem Iudicii title, would have clarified authority over the matter, but the Senate had declined it.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel espionage ring was revealed to span the territories adjoining the Bay, feeding the Salt Council.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: it was where the Empire first found proof of Grendel espionage, a ring since wound up.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Sign of Tamar there was cited as an example of a place resonant with particular constellations.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War and the Shuttered Lantern had earlier closed a Grendel spy ring there.
t.Spiral: Spiral hosted a Grendel jewel that could be destroyed by Senate motion, or used by the Military Council to lure or deter Grendel attacks on the territory over the next two seasons.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the accusing DuSesna Guild was of Tassatan extraction, and Tassato's senator was condemned for seconding the fane motion.

r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulian's shifting Night-touched streets and walking dramaturgical personae made it a place of intrigue, and it held the Grendel espionage jewel awaiting an Imperial decision.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Black Plateau seemed untouched by the rising Night magic, and false reports of a commission to trigger it could be used to deter Grendel attacks on Spiral.

Ratify Coiled Krait Treaty.d: Under the proposed treaty the Empire would have declared the Coiled Krait foreigners with all the protections of Imperial law, and ceded a town where they could make homes and live freely, safe from their kinfolk. In return the Coiled Krait would have given the Empire militarily significant information to aid its campaign in the Sarangrave. They would not take up arms against the Druj, but would offer other help that season before leaving for their new home. They also agreed to be bound by Imperial law and to end slavery among their people once they crossed into Imperial lands. The Senate did not ratify the treaty.

n.Druj: The Coiled Krait, a sept that had broken from the Banded Snake clan, sought refuge from its own kin and offered intelligence against the Druj. The failed vote left them without Imperial protection or a promised town.

t.Sarangrave: The treaty would have given the Empire militarily significant information for its campaign in the Druj-held Sarangrave, but the motion failed and the treaty was never ratified.

Restore the Throne Room.d: Proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by Mitwold, the motion followed the opportunity described in the Dog days are over Wind of Fortune. The motion credits the Castellan of Spiral Castle and houses of Dawn with securing the resources. After the Summer Solstice, several citizens, including Tallis Hart, Berith Relieur, Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Morien de Carsenere, donated white granite, crowns and thrones. Once complete, the restoration reduced the cost of upgrading Dawnish congregations by one white granite for a year, to a minimum of one wain. Hugh de Veran would complete and publish historical research into the pre-Imperial monarchs of Dawn.

n.Dawn: Dawn's ancient throne room was restored. This lowered the cost of upgrading Dawnish congregations for a year and led to published research on the nation's pre-Imperial monarchs.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle is thanked for helping to secure the resources for the restoration.

t.Astolat: The Castle of Thorns, a fortification in Astolat, had its throne room restored after a motion proposed by Astolat's own senator.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle is credited with helping to secure the restoration's costs.

r.Astolat/Withy: The throne room of the Castle of Thorns in Withy was restored over three months using 15 white granite and 45 crowns.

Root and branch.d: Five armies marched from the Barrens with Knights of Glory sent by Eleonaris and guided by Navarr from the Last Battle Wayhouse. They took Turan from Het Trakaa, bridged the river and pressed most of the way into Kroll. In the south, four armies secured Bloodwater Marsh and were about halfway through the Whisperwood, while the Citadel Guard's Glass Labyrinth ensnared the Druj. The Druj invasion of Lustri cut those four southern armies off from supply. Former slaves vanished with the help of the spirit Reedleaper, and an unexplained Wooden Fastness stood in Nesustak Forest. Battle opportunities followed at the Palace of the Sleepers and in Proceris.

n.Dawn: The Gryphon's Pride and the new Lions of Adelmar fought in the north, where the Lions held the Kroll riverbank during the crossing and drew the Black Wind's hatred. Some Dawnish warriors died gloriously striking at the God in the Lake, and Druj with heralds of Arhallogen threatened the Last Battle Wayhouse in Dawn's Barrens.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Turan Flats and Bloodwater Marsh, and their armies in Sarangrave were caught in the Glass Labyrinth. They seized Lustri and burned Stork's Gaze, but both their forces now face supply problems, and the Sept of Masks unleashed a monstrous creature to defend the Palace of the Sleepers.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar marched with the northern force, and its Highborn first spotted the caged captives and the rising horror at the lake. The Citadel Guard wove the Glass Labyrinth that trapped the Druj armies, but they are among the four southern armies now cut off from supply.
n.Navarr: Pathfinders of the Last Battle striding guided the northern advance, and the Quiet Step came from Reikos to join the southern force, which is now cut off. A Druj band threatened the Last Battle Wayhouse; its loss would expose Navarr resources in the Barrens to the foreign nation penalty.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost Lustri, and the garrison of Stork's Gaze died holding the fortification, sending a final heliopticon message of 'remember us'. Vigilance encouraged by the Urizen Assembly's mandate largely confined the invasion to Lustri.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle fought in the north alongside Ser Gaspare's knights, and its scouts were ambushed by a giant marsh octopus. The Golden Axe drew the Black Wind south and is now among the cut-off southern armies.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the armies set out after the Golden Magicians fayre in Astolat, and lumber collected there built the pontoon bridge into Kroll.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: it is cited as a place where being ambushed by the dread of the Druj miasma is half expected.
t.Morrow: The Towerjacks withdrew from Sarangrave to Morrow to help complete a fortification. There they met the Quiet Step marching to war.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Hunting Scorpion's Amber Scorpion sept once held Ossium, and its woods are listed among lands the orcs have polluted.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step came down from Reikos to fight in Sarangrave, and its woods are listed among lands the orcs have polluted.
t.Sarangrave: The Empire now holds Turan Flats and Bloodwater Marsh, while the Druj hold the rest apart from vallorn-held Bendol. The territory lay under Rivers of Life and the Druj miasma, and its trapped Druj armies cannot move more than one territory.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens flourished under Dawn while the Rahvin held the Bitter Strand and Navarr settled near their orc allies, to the Karass's resentment. Five armies marched through to invade Sarangrave, and Druj with heralds of Arhallogen now threaten the Last Battle Wayhouse.
t.Therunin: Almost all the Druj armies that ravaged the Navarr marshes left Therunin to invade Zenith, and the Black Wind left to defend Sarangrave. Great Forest Orcs and Navarr on the Barrens border are preparing for the vallorn's spread there.
t.Zenith: A major Druj host claimed Lustri and destroyed Stork's Gaze, with the Tainted Basilisk now able to focus rituals on the territory. The invaders made only about a tenth of the progress needed to claim Proceris, and a battle opportunity arose there.

r.Morrow/Peregro: The Towerjacks arrived with their tools to help complete the fortification being built in Peregro.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: the river crossed into Kroll flows south through Bendol, which remains under the vallorn and blocks the southern armies' route north.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: The southern Imperial force conquered Bloodwater Marsh after the Druj defence collapsed. The Bloodwater Spears had abandoned their homes in orderly fashion, leaving only a carving of a horned hare.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: The northern force bridged the river and is over four-fifths of the way to taking Kroll, with only the Palace of the Sleepers outside its control. There the Sept of Masks drowned Imperial captives and raised the colossal one-eyed God in the Lake, and an opportunity arose to stop the Palace's contents being spirited away.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: An unexplained Wooden Fastness here aided neither side and seemed to shelter allies of the Shacklebreaker. Fleeing Banded Snakes took refuge here, and a former slave hinted that something was happening in the forest.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Thornfen remains in Druj hands, hemming in the southern Imperial armies from the east. The garrison of its great fortification fought to defend Kroll.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Five armies with Knights of Glory stormed the Turan Flats and took the settlement of Turan, despite Het Trakaa's tortured souls and the Black Wind. The Banded Snakes scattered.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: The southern force pursued the Druj into the Whisperwood, toward the Thornwasp palace at Uklead, and is about halfway to taking the region. It found many traps but no supernatural ward.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Rahvin control the Bitter Strand, admitting only those who helped them survive and busily building homes and forging mithril and iron weapons.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: flowers bloomed across Dawnguard as summer came to the Barrens.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: flowers bloomed across Murderdale as summer came to the Barrens.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Navarr settled near the Last Battle Wayhouse, where the armies rested before invading. A Druj band with heralds of Arhallogen now threatens the wayhouse, and the Keeper of the Last Battle is charged with stopping it.
r.The Barrens/The Carmine Fields: Mentioned in passing: flowers bloomed across the Carmine Fields as summer came to the Barrens.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: The Druj armies that ravaged the Navarr marshes launched their invasion of Zenith out of East Ashes.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Druj overran Lustri, destroyed Stork's Gaze and smashed any spires they captured, and the Tainted Basilisk are believed to be here. Spires that had been warned through the Urizen Assembly's mandate fended off raiders, and the Champion of Vigilance may intercept a returning Druj band.
r.Zenith/Occursion: A few Druj patrols probed into Occursion to test the defenders but achieved little.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Druj are about a tenth of the way to claiming Proceris. A vanguard with Spring heralds is carrying a larval egg sac toward its marshes, and heroes have the chance to destroy or poison the sac and slay Orbubus the Weeper.

Shovels and spades.d: Under new general Jack Ashton, the Tusks steadily reclaimed the Chalkdowns. They were aided by the Thorn of the Ancestors' servants in Alderly and twenty heralds of Janon, who stirred grumbling over the Guerdon. The Jotun remain penned at Farstrider's Watch in Greensward. In Bregasland the Jotun swept into Ottermire within an hour. Queen Yrsa hunts the Strong Reeds, with a bounty on their general, and keeps Stephen of Sarcombe on a short leash. Bregas resentment towards the Empire eased. Conjunctions offer chances to seize Jotun mithril and rescue Marcher orcs. A battle opportunity offers a chance to stop a Mountain Bulwark renewing the Burhfæst at Graven Rock and to rescue the Clake family.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Strong Reeds are said to be harder to root out than a spy network or a ring of Grendel agents.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost the Chalkdowns but hold Greensward and Farstrider's Watch, and completed their conquest of Bregasland. Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir hunts the Strong Reeds and a new Mountain Bulwark marches to renew the Burhfæst.
n.The Marches: The Tusks reclaimed the Chalkdowns while the Strong Reeds hold out in conquered Bregasland. Marcher orcs are taking up arms, heralds of Janon stoke grievances over the Guerdon, and Marcher Pride and Loyalty grow stronger.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland fell entirely to the Jotun with Ottermire's capture, though the Strong Reeds organise hidden resistance. Bregas bitterness towards the Empire has subsided, and copies of the Life of Tom Drake circulate in secret.
t.Mitwold: With the Chalkdowns reclaimed, the Black Canal will give its full benefit to businesses and farms in Mitwold. The Burhfæst at Graven Rock has given the Jotun a vantage point over the territory.
t.Mournwold: The Tusks liberated the Chalkdowns, leaving only Greensward under Jotun control. Conjunctions offer chances to seize Jotun mithril and rescue Marcher orcs hunted by the Ulvenwar.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Igya Olgafsdottir, Jarl of Tromsa, was reportedly seen visiting the Ice Fishers at the Burhfæst in Bregasland.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's rich farmlands are evoked as what people usually imagine of the Marches.

r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Jotun swept into Ottermire and took the town in less than an hour, offering the Choice and completing their conquest of Bregasland.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: Strong Reeds sympathisers hide in The Rushes, and a Mountain Bulwark can be intercepted on the Cinder Drove before it reaches Graven Rock. Rescuing the captive Clakes from Jarl Aertha would end the region's resentful mood.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Servants of the Thorn of the Ancestors harried the Jotun here. A Jotun warband that retreated into Alderly was found strangled in a bramble hedge, its weapons gone.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Tusks pushed the Jotun out of the Chalkdowns step by step, and by the Summer Solstice the region was Imperial once more.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Greensward remains in Jotun hands, including Farstrider's Watch, the Singing Caves and Honour's Rest. Conjunctions offer chances to ambush a mithril caravan and rescue Marcher orcs hunted by the Ulvenwar.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Mentioned in passing: since the Empire conquered Southmoor, Jotun mithril caravans have had to take careful routes through Marcher lands.

Sing a song.d: The Great Library stands in Mourning Hollow in Summersend, built around Terunael ruins and a regio that once cycled between Day and Night. Until 388YE, priests may encourage Wise pilgrimages there, giving up three liao a season for four extra Synod votes and joining the Wisdom Assembly. The Singer of the Silence now gains Prismatic Ink and Crystal Fire each season, an obscured aura, and can use materials in place of crystal mana for mastered Day or Night rituals. Through Declarations of Alignment, the Conclave could align the regio to Phaleron by day and Sung by night. This would unlock Librarian's Incense and Pearlescent Wine and grant single uses of each eternal's protection in Hercynia. Such gifts would be hard to revoke.

n.Navarr: The Great Library that helped the Navarr solve the vallorn now has true Wisdom consecration in their Hercynian lands, and the proposed alignments could bring eternal protection or concealment to Navarr-held Hercynia.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a fane is noted as being built for Sung at Apulian in the League's territory of Spiral.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named, alongside the Empire, as the only nearby power able to perform the magnitude 200 Day ritual needed to pierce Sung's shroud.

t.Hercynia: Pilgrims may travel to the newly consecrated Great Library in Hercynia. If the Conclave agrees, Phaleron could protect the library once from attack, and Sung could once hide a single Imperial commission in the territory from all spying eyes.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: a fane to Sung is being built at Apulian in Spiral.

r.Hercynia/Summersend: The Great Library at Mourning Hollow in Summersend now carries a true Wisdom aura, and its Day-Night regio could be aligned to Phaleron by day and Sung by night if the Conclave so declares.

Smile like you mean it.d: The Free Folk are former Marracossan slaves who settled around Caer Faucon in Astolat with the help of the House of the Proffered Hand. They erected effigies to Lady Eleanor and debated three paths. The first was supporting the Lions of Adelmar. The second was aiding Dawnish efforts to spread the Way in Asavea as spies, saboteurs and missionaries. The third was strengthening the Proffered Hand network within and beyond the Empire. Each path drew objections from Dawnish and Highborn voices. Holding that they must move as one, the Free Folk will follow Synod judgements, especially from the Dawnish Assembly or the General Assembly. Prognostication proved impossible.
